title: BR trust-anchor list distribution, revocation push, and periodic node fetch absent (spec 06-security 8.7)
description:
Spec 06-security.md §8.7 (lines ~210-233): BR records (derived IID, PubKey) in a trust anchor list, distributes anchors to other nodes via CoAP; revocation = remove from list + push updated list to all managed nodes (+ optional signed broadcast); nodes SHOULD fetch updates periodically (e.g. every hour) or on BR announcement.

Requirements: R-06-035 (revocation via anchor-list push), R-06-036 (periodic fetch) in docs/spec-coverage/06-security-part1.md. Classification: not-implemented.

Evidence: no anchor-list CoAP resource, no push mechanism, no periodic fetcher in rust/, python/src/, or lichen/ (rg 'anchor' hits are persistence rollback anchors only). Local revocation flag exists in Python only (python/src/lichen/crypto/trust.py:709-729, tested python/tests/crypto/test_trust.py:372-411) and is not wired to any distribution path. BR-provisioned trust LEVEL exists everywhere (rust/lichen-gateway/src/trust.rs:672-713 BrProvisioned; python trust.py add_trust_anchor; C gcp_trust.h PROVISIONED) — what is missing is the distribution/revocation/fetch machinery that makes BR-provisioned fleets manageable.

Classification note: spec text is capability-form ('the border router can revoke...') with one SHOULD (periodic fetch), so filed as SHOULD-gap that breaks the documented BR-provisioned feature rather than a MUST violation.

Suggested placement: CoAP resource on BR for anchor-list fetch + revocation push (mirroring tunnel-auth/capability-announce patterns in spec 8.11/8.12), plus a periodic fetch/announcement hook on nodes; wire python revocation flag into it.
